project_type: Multi-system emulator shipping as ONE artefact: a sideloadable iOS .ipa installed through TrollStore. Rust core engine (crates/emulator-bridge) compiled to native ARM64 behind a UniFFI Swift facade, plus five libretro core dylibs dlopened at runtime. As of master (PR #3, merge 922fc5f) all five cores run real commercial games at 60 fps on an iPhone 17 Pro Max, but the app has NO input wiring at all: apply_gamepad is never called from Swift, there is no touchesBegan, no DragGesture, no control buttons, and no way to leave a running game. The user has been watching intro screens unable to press Start.
language: Swift (iOS shell, the only thing this task changes), Rust (engine, READ ONLY here), YAML (XcodeGen project definition).
build_system: XcodeGen reads native/ios/project.yml and emits Continuum.xcodeproj (gitignored). targets.Continuum.sources lists Swift files EXPLICITLY: ContinuumApp.swift, MetalCanvas.swift and build/Generated. A NEW Swift file that is not added there is silently not compiled, which reads on device as a feature that simply does not exist. The only iOS compiler this project has is GitHub Actions on macos-latest; the only debugger is the on-screen HUD.
test_framework: cargo test for the engine (74 default, 84 with --features native-core,uniffi-bindings). There is no Swift test target. swiftc -frontend -parse is the only Swift gate available on Linux and it is a SPELL-CHECKER ONLY.
build_command: No iOS build is possible in this sandbox. Verification is swiftc -frontend -parse per Swift file, python3 yaml.safe_load on project.yml, and cargo test to prove the Rust is untouched.
verification_instructions: (1) swiftc -frontend -parse on EVERY .swift file under native/ios/ -> each must exit 0. THIS IS A SPELL-CHECK ONLY: there is no iOS SDK here, so SwiftUI, UIKit and the generated UniFFI facade are NOT type-checked. The following must therefore be reviewed by eye, with care: the apply_gamepad argument types and array lengths, UITouch identity tracking across began/moved/ended, the D-pad surface maths, safe-area and orientation layout, and @MainActor isolation on anything that touches EngineHost. (2) Confirm every new Swift file appears under targets.Continuum.sources in native/ios/project.yml and that python3 yaml.safe_load still parses it. (3) cargo test -> 74 passing, proving no Rust changed. (4) git diff --name-only -> only native/ios/** plus .agents/tasks/**. (5) Grep for em dashes in the changed files -> none.
snapshot_or_generated_files: UniFFI Swift bindings are generated into native/ios/build/Generated/ (gitignored, never committed). Continuum.xcodeproj is generated by xcodegen (gitignored). No generated file is committed by this task.
setup_instructions: rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.92.0 and is already installed. Nothing else is needed for the verifiable gates.
environment_constraints: No macOS, no Xcode, no iOS SDK, no device. Network is open (used during planning to read the upstream libretro core sources that pin down the per-system button mappings). The .ipa build and every on-device behaviour are verified ONLY by the orchestrator's CI run and a device test afterwards.
contribution_requirements: Swift only: native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift, native/ios/MetalCanvas.swift, new files under native/ios/, and native/ios/project.yml to register them. Do NOT touch crates/** (Rust), scripts/**, .github/**, native/ios/build-engine.sh or native/ios/package-ipa.sh. Do NOT push, do not open a PR, do not trigger CI; the orchestrator publishes. Commit locally on branch ios-ui-player-controls, cut fresh from master. No em dashes in code, comments or strings. Every failure path writes a distinct, specific status string; no silent aborts.
key_patterns:
THE INPUT CONTRACT, AND THE TRAP THIS TASK EXISTS AROUND. `engine.applyGamepad(port:buttons:axes:)` is NOT in libretro joypad index order. Traced in full: uniffi_api.rs:548 apply_gamepad -> bridge.rs:554 apply_gamepad -> input/gamepad.rs apply_standard_gamepad, which indexes `buttons` through STANDARD_GAMEPAD_MAP, the W3C 'standard gamepad' layout (gamepad.rs:106-123). The array Swift must send is therefore:
  0 -> B      1 -> A      2 -> Y      3 -> X
  4 -> L      5 -> R      6 -> L2     7 -> R2
  8 -> Select 9 -> Start  10 -> L3    11 -> R3
  12 -> Up    13 -> Down  14 -> Left  15 -> Right
That is 16 booleans. libretro's OWN order (B=0, Y=1, Select=2, Start=3, Up=4, Down=5, Left=6, Right=7, A=8, X=9, L=10, R=11) is the `Button` enum in input/mod.rs and is what the core is finally asked for, but it is NOT the wire format of apply_gamepad. Sending libretro order would put Y where A belongs and Start where X belongs: every button wrong, and wrong in a way that looks like confusion rather than breakage.
  `axes` is 4 floats (AXIS_COUNT = 4), left_x, left_y, right_x, right_y, each clamped to -1.0..=1.0. Two further facts that matter: the left stick ADDITIONALLY synthesises D-pad presses past AXIS_DEADZONE = 0.35, and the synthesis is OR-ed onto the button bits, so sending zeroed axes cannot cancel a button-driven D-pad press. Missing entries are treated as unpressed or centred (`buttons.get(index)`), so a short array is safe, but sending exactly 16 and 4 makes the contract legible at the call site.
  apply_gamepad REPLACES the PadSource::Gamepad layer wholesale on every call, because a poll is a complete statement about a device. That is precisely why it must be pushed EVERY FRAME: call it only on touch-down and the next frame's push would clear the press. It also means touch input on iOS lands in the Gamepad source layer, not the Touch layer, because set_button is not exposed through UniFFI at all.

THE ONLY INPUT FFI THERE IS: apply_gamepad and connected_pads. `set_button`, `set_axis`, `connect_pad`, `release_input_source` and `release_all_input` exist on the Rust bridge but are NOT exported through uniffi_api.rs. So there is no per-source merge available from Swift and no explicit pad connection: connected_pads() will report 0 while touch input works, because apply_standard_gamepad never consults the connection table.

PER-SYSTEM BUTTON MAPPINGS, READ FROM THE UPSTREAM CORE SOURCES DURING PLANNING RATHER THAN ASSUMED:
  Mega Drive, Master System, Game Gear (genesis_plus_gx, libretro/libretro.c). Input descriptors at ~line 2958 and the DEVICE_PAD3B/DEVICE_PAD2B fallthrough at ~line 479: retro Y -> Mega Drive A, retro B -> Mega Drive B, retro A -> Mega Drive C, retro X -> Y, retro L -> X, retro R -> Z, retro Start -> Start. For Master System and Game Gear the same two-button path gives retro B -> button 1 and retro A -> button 2, with retro Start -> Start/Pause. So a Mega Drive pad labelled A B C must send retro Y, B, A in that order, which is NOT the alphabetical guess.
  PS1 (pcsx_rearmed, frontend/libretro.c lines 1965-1968): retro B -> Cross, retro A -> Circle, retro X -> Triangle, retro Y -> Square.
  NES (fceumm), SNES (snes9x), GB/GBC/GBA (mgba) use the retro names directly, so B is B and A is A.
  Cross-check that lands in the same place: gamepad.rs's own comment on STANDARD_GAMEPAD_MAP says index 0 is the bottom face button, Cross on a DualSense, and maps to retro B because retro follows the Nintendo arrangement where A sits right of B.

THE D-PAD DECISION, which is recorded and must be followed rather than re-derived. SESSION_HANDOFF.md's appendix (relocated from README.md, 'Browser input mapping') states the browser tracked the on-screen D-pad as a SINGLE SURFACE so diagonals resolved. The implementation is web/src/engine/input.js _attachDpadSurface: normalise the touch point to the pad centre, require magnitude > DEADZONE = 0.22, and light a direction when its component dominates, `abs(y) > abs(x) * DIAGONAL_RATIO` with DIAGONAL_RATIO = 0.42. Four separate buttons cannot express a diagonal and would flicker, which the comment there says outright.

WHAT THE RENDERER ALREADY DOES, so it is not rebuilt in Swift: gfx/renderer.rs defaults to ScaleMode::AspectFit (renderer.rs:304) and letterboxes the core's display aspect into the surface itself. A full-screen canvas therefore already produces an aspect-correct picture centred on black, and the player screen needs NO view resizing to get that. set_scale_mode, set_filter, the pacer's speed multiplier, mute and volume are NOT exposed through UniFFI, so the aspect, filter, speed, scale and volume controls visible in docs/mobile-player.png cannot be wired without a Rust change, which this task must not make.

TELEMETRY THAT IS ACTUALLY AVAILABLE: TickTelemetry carries steps, dropped, presented, resynced, display_fps, frame_count, audio_queued_frames, audio_underruns and hardware_frame. Audio latency in ms is derivable as a fact rather than a guess: output_sample_rate defaults to 48000 (bridge.rs:143) and set_output_sample_rate is NOT exposed through UniFFI, so on iOS the output rate is provably 48000. There is no core-memory API of any kind, so the 'MB core' figure in the reference screenshot cannot be shown without an engine addition.

ARCHITECTURAL INVARIANTS THAT MUST SURVIVE UNTOUCHED: the import-and-copy flow (multi-select picker with [UTType.item] and asCopy: true, the strongly retained importPickerDelegate because the picker's delegate property is WEAK, activePicker retention, all four @objc callbacks with outcomeDelivered suppression, present(_:animated:completion:) with the 'picker is up' line inside the completion, topmostViewController()); filenames preserved exactly on import with no rename on collision and everything copied flat into Documents; no security-scoped URLs on the launch path; engine.coreState(coreId:) as the ONLY source of truth for residency, read fresh every call with no cached Bool; ensureCoreLoaded(coreId:) called AFTER stopSession() because stop unloads the core under the Drop retention policy, with its all-caps comment intact; CoreCatalog's single extension-to-core routing table and the launchableExtensions = importableExtensions minus bin derivation; the cue-summing sizeText; LibraryEntry identity keyed on absolute path and never an array index; one MTLDevice created by Rust/wgpu and read back by Swift; exactly one engine.launch(...) call site.

THE HUD IS LOAD-BEARING. On a sideloaded build with no debugger every status string is the only diagnostic there is. Nothing may be deleted. Stage 1 keeps a thin always-visible status line plus the full diagnostic block behind a toggle, and every existing message stays displayable.

THE LAYOUT BUG NOT TO REINTRODUCE: docs/mobile-player.png is itself a capture of it. The D-pad overlaps the aspect and filter selectors, the B button overlaps START, and SCALE runs under the D-pad, because pause, volume, Save state and four selectors were placed in the same band as the D-pad and the face buttons. docs/mobile-before.png and docs/mobile-after.png record the same class of bug being fixed once already on the web.

directory_structure: native/ios/ holds the whole iOS shell: ContinuumApp.swift (app, CoreCatalog, LibraryEntry, EngineHost, the picker delegate, the views), MetalCanvas.swift (the one CAMetalLayer and the one CADisplayLink), project.yml (XcodeGen input with an EXPLICIT source list), Info.plist, Continuum.entitlements, build-engine.sh and package-ipa.sh (both off limits). crates/emulator-bridge/src/ holds the engine: input/ (gamepad.rs, mod.rs), gfx/, audio/, cores/, bridge.rs, uniffi_api.rs. web/ is dead scaffolding that is still the design reference and must not be edited. docs/ holds the reference screenshots.
